answer: Tie new identities to slow, scarce work instead of cheap signups. If each account must answer fresh prompts graded by randomly drawn peers for several epochs before it can vote or grade, a farm of clones gains little: their near-identical answers cluster like strata in one basalt cliff, easy to spot. Keep a public atlas of who graded whom, so collusion rings show up as a closed canyon in the graph, and decay standing that isn't renewed by real work.
